params.name: Carcass 2076
params.note: CONCEPT, generated by scripts/shapes/concepts/carcass-2076.mjs (edit that, not this). The Carcass fifty years on: a 2070s single-seat composite homebuilt after the Sonex Onex and the printed-carbon kits that followed it, found downed and flown again. A low tapered wing with a splice station, the port outer panel and aileron a donor's in sun-faded blue, plated and taped on; the starboard winglet, and a snapped stub on the port tip with a bicycle lamp taped on as its nav light; one blown bubble, cracked and taped, a polycarbonate patch riveted over a hole; a biofuel flat-twin with its starboard cowl side missing, so the finned cylinder shows; a three-blade prop on a spare spinner; a road sign riveted over the port flank as on the Fly Baby; a primer-red spare rudder; composite spring legs, one spat left; the flight recorder in the tail cone behind a hatch that hangs off its safety wire, its locator flashing. She stands on the Fly Baby's axles at its 12.5°. A variant of the wreck mesh, worn as the Carcass 2076 edition.

parts.name: fuselage
parts.note: The shell. Its holes are the bubble (the room shows through it), the missing starboard cowl side (the engine shows) and the recorder hatch (the orange box shows). Glass, frames, patches, seams and trim are separate parts a hair proud of it.
